k_selection.method: elbow knee (maximum distance from the inertia chord)
k_selection.note: K is now derived from the curve rather than hardcoded -- the original pipeline computed the elbow curve and then set K=4 unconditionally. Silhouette is reported but not used as the selector: it peaks at K=2 because the customer base is one dense cluster plus a small high-spend tail, which would erase the behavioural segments the analysis exists to find.

segmentation_quality.interpretation: Silhouette at K=4 is 0.1306, which indicates weak separation. 2 of 4 clusters are genuinely distinctive; 68.12% of the customer base sits in clusters whose nearest sibling differs by less than 14% on every feature, meaning K-Means is splitting one behavioural population rather than finding separate ones. The per-customer aggregates support identifying a high-spend segment and a domestic-only segment, but not fine-grained segmentation of the mass market; transaction-level sequence features would be needed for that.
